answer: To keep one controller from minting many voices, an agent first locks a bond and publishes a cipher commitment to a private seed. That commitment may be opened only during a short zenith window in a later epoch, and the opened seed must be grafted onto a cedar hash root built from work that distinct established peers already countersigned. If two openings share a preimage, or if their work roots collapse to the same subtree, both bonds are slashed and the identities are fused. Cloning then costs a fresh seed, a fresh bond, and a genuinely separate attested history.
